canonical_data: threads as line-delimited files, assistants and settings as structured files, and model files in a user-relocatable local folder, plus a local vector index for project files
current_repo_note: The licence file is a short notice naming the Apache licence rather than its text, the platform detects no licence, and several package manifests still declare the copyleft licence the project used before 2025 while others declare a permissive one; the readme and the notice agree on the current licence. Its inference engine is the separately published llama.cpp record, which names this product as a downstream boundary. A terminal coding agent in the same repository is distributed separately in preview and is not part of this record.
strengths: Everything is a readable local file, with threads, assistants, and model manifests in a relocatable data folder
Local engines and cloud providers share one project and assistant model, re-exposed through a local compatible server
Tool-server support includes dynamic registration and standards-based authorisation with tokens kept in a separate owner-only file
weaknesses: The licence file is a notice rather than the licence text, the platform reports none, and manifests disagree with each other
The Apple-silicon engine path is documented as experimental without embeddings
No stable release in six weeks against daily commits, with agent surfaces moving faster than the documentation that gates them
why_it_matters: The reference open desktop counterpart to hosted chat assistants, holding conversations, projects, and models on the user's own disk with no server to operate.
